translations.text: Joshua secretly sent two young men as spies from Shittim and told them, “Go up and inspect the land and Jericho.” The two young men went and entered Jericho. They entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there.
The woman took the two men and hid them. She said, “The men did come to me, but I did not know where they were from.”
Joshua said to the Israelites, “Come here and hear the word of the Lord our God.”

The priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s law stood firmly on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All the Israelites crossed over on dry ground until the entire people had finished crossing the Jordan.
He commanded them to take twelve round stones from there, from the middle of the Jordan where the priests’ feet stood: “Carry them with you and keep them in your camps, where you stay tonight.”
On that day the Lord made Joshua great before all the people of Israel, and they feared him as they had feared Moses, throughout his lifetime.
They ate from the produce of the land, unleavened bread and fresh grain.
While Joshua was in Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua approached him and said, “Are you one of our people or one of our enemies?”
Seven priests shall carry seven jubilee horns before the ark. On the seventh day they shall circle the city seven times, and the priests shall blow those horns.
As Joshua had told the people, the seven priests took seven sacred trumpets to go before the Lord. As they went, they blew loudly as a signal, and the ark of the Lord’s law followed them.
The Lord was with Joshua, and his name became known throughout the whole land.
About three thousand of the people went up, but the men of Ai drove them back, and they fled before them.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, together with the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying facedown?”
They brought them out of his tent and took them to Joshua and all the elders of Israel, and laid them before the Lord.
Joshua saw that those who had lain in ambush had captured the city. They knew it when they saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. Then they turned back and killed the people of Ai.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
All those who died at that time, men and women, numbered twelve thousand—all the people of Ai.

When all the kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan heard of it—those in the mountains, those in the wilderness, those along the entire shore of the Great Sea, and those in the Anti-Lebanon—the Hittites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Amorites, Girgashites, and Jebusites;
Now you are cursed. There shall never cease to be slaves among you who cut wood and draw water for me and for my God.
Joshua came upon them suddenly at night, having departed from Gilgal.

The sun and the moon stood still in their positions where they were, until the Lord destroyed their enemies. This was written in this book at that time. The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not move toward the west for a whole day.
After this, when Joshua and all Israel had finished killing them in a very great slaughter beyond counting, those of them who escaped fled and entered fortified towns.

They also captured Makkedah that day and killed its people and its king with the sword. They destroyed every living person in it and left no one breathing there, not even one; no one escaped. They did to the king of Makkedah as they had done to the king of Jericho.
The Lord delivered Lachish into the hands of Israel. They captured it on the second day, killed its people with the sword, and destroyed it as they had done to Libnah.
They struck it with the sword, together with every living person in it, and no one escaped. As they had done to Adullam, they destroyed it together with everyone in it.
All their kings gathered and came together, joining forces to fight Israel by the waters of Merom.
The Israelites took all its plunder for themselves. But they slaughtered all the people, destroying them with the sword, and left not a single living person among them.
From Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad and the fields of Lebanon toward Mount Hermon, he captured all their kings, killed them, and destroyed them.

And the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, on its eastern side, along the road toward Jeshimoth, and southward below Medoth and Pisgah.
The king of Jerusalem; the king of Hebron.
All who live in the mountains, from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim [?], all the Sidonians—I will destroy them before the Israelites, as I told you.
And Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Seradoth, and Zion on Mount Enab.

And in Adom, Otrga, and Abayin [?], and Succoth and Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon; and the Jordan and their border as far as one end of the Sea of Chinnereth, across the Jordan on the east.

And half the land of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the towns of Og’s kingdom in Bashan, belonged to the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh—to half the descendants of Machir, the son of Manasseh, according to their clans.
It goes toward Azmon and comes out at the valley of Egypt. Their boundary ends at the sea. This is their southern boundary.

Their boundary goes up through the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, south of Jebus, which is Jerusalem. Their boundary comes out at the summit of the mountain facing the Valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the land of the Rephaim.
Their boundary passes westward from Baal and passes along the boundary of Asaretus, south of the town of Jearim and north of Chesalon. It descends toward the town of Eliu and passes toward Libah.
Caleb son of Jephunneh drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Talmai, and Ahiman.
And the towns of Hezron, that is, Hazor.
And Jarmuth, Adullam, Mamre, Socoh, and Azekah.
And Adalel, Mizpah, Joktheel, and Makesa.
And Gedor, Bogadiel, Naamah, and Makkedah: sixteen towns and their villages.
And Humtah, Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, and Zior: nine towns and their hills.
The descendants of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, received their inheritance.
From Tappuah their boundary goes westward along Kanah and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their clans.
And the towns set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh—all their towns and their villages.

And an allotment fell to the remaining descendants of Manasseh according to their clans: to the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Asriel, the descendants of Shechem, and the descendants of Hepher.
These were their males according to their clans.
The descendants of Manasseh could not destroy these cities, and the Canaanites came and lived in that land.
The descendants of Joseph addressed Joshua and said to him, “Why have you given us only one inheritance and one measured portion, when I am a numerous people and the Lord has blessed me?”
They said, “The hill country of Ephraim is not enough for us, and the Canaanites who live in it have choice horses and iron at Beth-shean and in its surrounding villages, in the valley of Jezreel.”
“For the field is yours. It is a forest, and you will clear it for yourself. It will be yours until you destroy the Canaanites, for they have choice horses, but you yourself are stronger than they.”
It passes to the spring of Beth-shemesh and goes to Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and descends to the stone of Bohan, of the descendants of Reuben.
It passes along the western side of Beth-arabah, and their boundary descends along the western side of the sea.
From the sea and Maralah, it joins Beth-arabah, which is in the valley opposite Jokneam.
It turns from Sarid toward the eastern side of Beth-shemesh, to the boundary of Chesulloth, passes through Daberath, and goes up to Japhia.
From there it passes along the eastern side of the city of Geber, which is toward the north, and passes to Rimmon of Amteryoza.
Their boundary passes to the west of Amoth, and its endpoint is at Jiphthah-el toward the south.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun according to their clans: the cities and their surrounding villages.
Their boundary turns into Ramah and extends to the spring of Misphat and the Tyrians. Their boundary turns into Iasiph, and the boundary ends at the sea, and from Leb and Achzib.
Their boundary was Mohalam, Mola, Besemiin, Arme, Nabo, and Iaphtheme, as far as Aodem, and its endpoint was the Jordan.

These are their portions, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel gave them as an inheritance, according to their allotments, at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of witness. And they went to divide the land.

He shall flee to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate, and tell his case to the elders of that city. The people shall take him in among them and give him a place, and he shall live with them.
They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “The Lord commanded through Moses that we should be given cities in which to live, and their pasturelands for our livestock.”
The tribe of the descendants of Judah, the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, and some from the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin gave these cities, which were named:
And from the clan of Issachar: Kishion and the land set apart with it, and Daberath and the land set apart with it.

“This is what the whole assembly of the Lord says: What is this offense that you have committed before the God of Israel, abandoning the Lord today and building yourselves an altar, so that you deny the Lord today?”
“It was only out of fear of the Lord that we did this, saying, ‘Lest in the future your children say to our children: What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?’”
“And we said, ‘Let us do this and build this altar, not for an offering and not for a sacrifice.’”

And we said, “If it happens in the future that they speak to us or to our children, they are to say to them, ‘Look at the likeness of the Lord’s altar that our ancestors made, not for offerings and not for sacrifices, but to be a witness between us and you.’”

When Phinehas the priest and all the representatives of the assembly and the leaders of Israel who were with him heard the words spoken to them by the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were quiet.

This report reassured the Israelites. When they told the Israelites, they blessed the God of the Israelites and said, “Then we will not go up against them to fight them and destroy the land of the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.” And they continued to live in it.
After this, many days after the Lord, the God of Israel, had given them rest from all their enemies around them, Joshua grew old and was advanced in years.
The people answered and said, “Far be it from us to abandon the Lord and worship other gods!”
Joshua said to the people, “You yourselves are witnesses against yourselves that you yourselves have chosen the Lord, to worship him.” And they said, “We are witnesses.”
